Rashi on Bekhorot 6a:13:1.hebrew: או דלמא כיון - דתרוייהו שוו, דמין בהמה טמאה נינהו, לאו שינויא יתירא הוא; וכי אית מקצת סימנים דאם — חייב:
Rashi on Bekhorot 6a:13:1.english: Or perhaps since - For both of them are alike in that they are a species of non-kosher animal, [so] it is not an excessive difference; and when it has some characteristics of the mother, [it is] obligated.

Rashi on Bekhorot 6a:14:1.hebrew: סימנין מילתא - חשובה היא, דאע"ג דאישתני כולי האי, מחייבי ליה מקצת סימנין בבכורה:
Rashi on Bekhorot 6a:14:1.english: Characteristics are a matter - [It is a] significant [matter], such that even though it has changed this much, partial characteristics obligate it in [the sanctity of] a firstborn:

Rashi on Bekhorot 6a:15:1.hebrew: מאי לאו אפי' פרה שילדה מין סוס - וש"מ סימנא מילתא היא, וכ"ש כולהו אינך:
Rashi on Bekhorot 6a:15:1.english: What, is it not even a cow that gave birth to a horse of sorts? - And conclude from this that [having] a characteristic is a significant matter, and all the more so all the other [cases].

Rashi on Bekhorot 6a:15:2.hebrew: לא אפרה שילדה מין חמור - דהואיל ותרוייהו בני קדושת בהמה נינהו, כי אית מקצת סימנין חייב, ולא תפשוט מינה אלא חדא:
Rashi on Bekhorot 6a:15:2.english: No, [it refers] to a cow that gave birth to a donkey of sorts - For since both of them are subject to the sanctity of a [firstborn] animal, when it has some [of the mother's] characteristics, it is obligated [in firstborn status]; and you can resolve from it only one [dilemma].

Rashi on Bekhorot 6a:16:1.hebrew: מאי לאו אתרוייהו - קאי האי "ואם יש מקצת סימנין", ותפשוט מינה תרתי:
Rashi on Bekhorot 6a:16:1.english: What, is it not [referring] to both of them - Does this [clause], “And if it has some characteristics,” apply [to both], and [thus] you can resolve two [dilemmas] from it?

Rashi on Bekhorot 6a:16:2.english: No, [it is referring] to a cow that gave birth to a donkey of sorts - And [this is] because both of them are sanctified with firstborn [sanctity]:

Rashi on Bekhorot 6a:17:1.hebrew: אבל חמור שילדה מין סוס למאי הלכתא קתני לה הכא לפטורא - לאשמעינן דנדמה הוי ופטור מן הבכורה כי לית ביה מקצת סימנין, דמשום רישא קתני חמור שילדה מין סוס, אבל סיפא לאו עלה מהדר:
Rashi on Bekhorot 6a:17:1.english: But [as for] a donkey that gave birth to a horse of sorts, for what halakha did it teach it here? To exempt [it]? - [Is it] to inform us that it is [considered] an offspring that resembles another species [nidmeh] and is exempt from [the sanctity of] the firstborn when it does not possess some of the [mother’s] characteristics — for it taught “a donkey that gave birth to a horse of sorts” [only] on account of the first clause, but the latter clause does not refer back to it?

Rashi on Bekhorot 6a:19:1.hebrew: חמור אדום - וליחייב בבכורה, קמ"ל. סתם סוסים אדומים הן:
Rashi on Bekhorot 6a:19:1.english: A red donkey - And let it be obligated in [the law of the] firstborn; [therefore,] it teaches us [that it is exempt]. Ordinary horses are red:

Rashi on Bekhorot 6a:1:1.hebrew: ת"ל - מקרא אחר (שמות ל״ד:כ׳): "ופטר חמור תפדה בשה". אם אינו ענין למעט שאר בהמה טמאה משה — שהרי מעטן בפסוק ראשון — תנהו ענין למעטן מכל קדושת בכור:
Rashi on Bekhorot 6a:1:1.english: The verse states - Another verse (Exodus 34:20): “And the firstborn of a donkey you shall redeem with a lamb.” If it is not needed to exclude other non-kosher animals from [redemption with] a lamb — for it already excluded them in the first verse — apply it to exclude them from all sanctity of a firstborn.

Rashi on Bekhorot 6a:21:1.hebrew: סימנא בעלמא - דלא תחליף לך גירסתך במשנה, ותימא: טהורה שילדה מין טמאה — אסור, וטמאה שילדה מין טהורה — מותר:
Rashi on Bekhorot 6a:21:1.english: It is merely a mnemonic - So that your version in the Mishnah not become reversed for you, and you [mistakenly] say: A kosher [animal] that gave birth to a non-kosher species is forbidden, and a non-kosher [animal] that gave birth to a kosher species is permitted.

Rashi on Bekhorot 6a:2:1.hebrew: מתקיף לה רב אחא - הא תרוייהו צריכי, דאי כתב חד — הוה אמינא: הוי פטר חמור דבר שהיה בכלל "בכור הבהמה הטמאה תפדה":
Rashi on Bekhorot 6a:2:1.english: Rav Aḥa objects to this - Both of them are needed; for if [the Merciful One] had written [only] one, I would say: A firstborn donkey is a matter that was included in the general rule of “the firstborn of an impure animal you shall redeem.”

Rashi on Bekhorot 6a:2:2.hebrew: ויצא מן הכלל ללמד - שפדיונו בשה — לא ללמד על עצמו יצא, אלא ללמד על הכלל כולו יצא כו', ולעולם נפדין בשה. ת"ל מקרא אחר: "ופטר חמור תפדה" — לומר לך: זה בשה, ולא אחר בשה:
Rashi on Bekhorot 6a:2:2.english: And emerged from the generalization to teach - That its redemption is with a lamb: "It did not emerge to teach concerning itself, but emerged to teach concerning the entire generalization, etc.," and indeed, [all non-kosher firstborns] are redeemed with a lamb. [Therefore,] Scripture states another verse: "And the firstborn of a donkey you shall redeem" — to tell you: this [one is redeemed] with a lamb, but another [is] not [redeemed] with a lamb.

Rashi on Bekhorot 6a:3:1.english: [The verse] excluded them from a lamb, but actually with any item - And [they are] sanctified as firstborns.

Rashi on Bekhorot 6a:4:1.hebrew: א"כ לכתוב - קרא תניינא: חמור בשה תפדה, ואנא ידענא דבפטר קמישתעי. מדהדר כתב פטר — ש"מ: מדין פטר רחם ממעט להו לשאר בהמות טמאות, דאין להם דין בכורה:
Rashi on Bekhorot 6a:4:1.english: If so, let [the Merciful One] write - [In] the second verse: "A donkey you shall redeem with a lamb," and I would know that it is speaking of a firstborn. Since it went back and wrote "firstborn," learn from this that it excludes other non-kosher animals from the law of an opener of the womb, that they have no law of firstborn status.

Rashi on Bekhorot 6a:6:1.hebrew: כל מקנך תזכר - פטר שור ושה, ופטר חמור תפדה בשה — כלל ופרט בהדדי:
Rashi on Bekhorot 6a:6:1.english: From all your livestock you shall take the males - [The verse continues:] “The firstborn of an ox and a sheep, and the firstborn of a donkey you shall redeem with a lamb” — [these constitute] a generalization and a detail together.

Rashi on Bekhorot 6a:7:1.hebrew: פטר חמור הפסיק הענין - דלא תדייניה בכלל ופרט. דאי אקרא קמא קא מהדר — מכדי כתיב לעיל מיניה "פטר שור ושה", לכתוב "וחמור תפדה בשה" ונהדר אפטר דלעיל; אלא מדהדר כתב "פטר", ש"מ: לאו אקרא קמא קמהדר:
Rashi on Bekhorot 6a:7:1.english: "The firstborn of a donkey" interrupts the matter - So that you should not expound it as a generalization and a detail. For if it were referring back to the first verse — seeing that it is written prior to it, "the firstborn of an ox and a sheep," let it write: "and a donkey you shall redeem with a lamb," and it would refer back to "firstborn" [mentioned] above. Rather, since it went back and wrote "firstborn," learn from this that it is not referring back to the first verse.

Rashi on Bekhorot 6a:7:2.hebrew: וי"ו - דכתב "ופטר", הדר ערביה ואהדריה אקרא קמא, דוי"ו מוסף על ענין ראשון:
Rashi on Bekhorot 6a:7:2.english: The [letter] vav - In that [the verse] wrote "and the firstborn," it went back and combined it, and linked it back to the first verse, for [the letter] vav adds to the preceding matter.

Rashi on Bekhorot 6a:8:1.hebrew: ור' יוסי - אמר לך: אי אקרא קמא קאי, לא לכתוב פטר לאפסוקיה, ולא נצטרך וי"ו לערביה:
Rashi on Bekhorot 6a:8:1.english: And Rabbi Yosei - [He could] say to you: If it refers back to the first verse, [the Torah] should not have written “firstborn” to interrupt it, and we would not have needed a vav to combine it.

Rashi on Bekhorot 6a:9:1.english: And then combines them - To say that we should expound it as a generalization and a detail.

Tosafot on Bekhorot 6a:20:1.hebrew: ומה הן באכילה - מה הוא מיושב יותר, שלא דבר אלא בפרה שילדה מין חמור, ולא חמור (הילד פרה):
Tosafot on Bekhorot 6a:20:1.english: "And what is their status with regard to consumption?" - How well-settled it is [now], that [the Mishnah] spoke only of a cow that gave birth to a donkey-type, and not a donkey (that gave birth to a cow).

Tosafot on Bekhorot 6a:20:2.hebrew: למה לי למיתני שהיוצא - לקמן דייק מינה: מי רגלים של חמור אסורין. והכא דייק מדקתני שהיוצא, שנותן טעם לדבר — הוה ליה למיתני והיוצא:
Tosafot on Bekhorot 6a:20:2.english: "Why do I need to teach 'that which emerges'" - Later [on 7b], [the Gemara] deduces from it that donkey urine is forbidden. But here, [the Gemara] infers [its question] from the fact that [the Mishnah] teaches "she-hayotzei" [for that which emerges], which gives a reason for the matter; [otherwise,] it should have taught "ve-hayotzei" [and that which emerges].
